definition: Hip-hop built on hard sampled kick and snare, usually lifted from vinyl and swung on an SP-1200 or MPC. The name imitates the drums.
Early-1990s West Coast rap style built on 1970s funk grooves, typically replayed by live musicians instead of sampled.
Hip-hop production built on sped-up, pitched-up vocal samples, named for Alvin and the Chipmunks.
An instrumental made in the style of a named artist and sold or leased online, often with non-exclusive rights.
A library of original loops composed by a 'sample producer' for other producers to build beats on.
New York drill that puts a recognizable R&B, pop or rap sample over drill drums; Complex gave it the name in print in May 2022.
Newark club style descended from Baltimore club: chopped samples, a triplet kick pattern and 808 bass.
1990s French house style that loops late-1970s and early-1980s disco samples under sweeping filter and phaser effects.
Breakbeat style built on the Amen break and other funk breaks, with basslines and vocal samples from dub, reggae and dancehall.
1990s style combining heavy breakbeats, acid-house synth loops, funk and rock samples and film or TV dialogue.
Label coined in Mixmag in June 1994 for downtempo, sample-based records such as DJ Shadow's; Portishead's Geoff Barrow has said he hated it.
John Oswald's term, from a 1985 essay, for music made openly from existing recordings.
A track that blends two or more existing songs, typically one song's vocal over another's instrumental.
Early-2010s internet genre made almost entirely of slowed-down samples of 1980s and 1990s smooth jazz, lounge and R&B.
DJ Screw's Houston technique of slowing records down and cutting them with skipped beats and scratching.
Internet-era slowed remixes with added reverb, spread on YouTube; critics tie the style to chopped and screwed.
A faster, higher-pitched edit of a song; labels began releasing official ones in 2022 and 2023 after fan edits spread on TikTok.
A Jamaican instrumental backing track made to be reused by many vocalists.
The rhythm under reggaeton, usually traced to Steely & Clevie's 1989 'Fish Market' riddim and named after Shabba Ranks' 'Dem Bow'.
The electronic bass sound that is amapiano's signature, usually credited to the producer MDU aka TRP.
Spotify feature announced in November 2025 that maps a track's samples, covers and collaborators, drawing on WhoSampled; in beta for Premium subscribers from March 2026.
Software that splits a finished mix into vocals, drums, bass and other parts; the most common AI use producers reported in 2024 and 2026 surveys.
An AI-made imitation of a real person's voice or likeness, the subject of the US NO FAKES Act bill.
The EU copyright exception AI developers rely on for training; the Munich court held it did not cover the memorized works in GEMA v. Suno.
A service whose AI outputs cannot be taken off the platform; the condition applied to Udio's existing product after its 2025 settlement with Universal.
